newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank says to watch financial markets.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank says to watch financial markets.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday it would keep a close eye on developments in financial markets in the future, as part of its observation of price developments.

The German central bank also said it believed a slowdown in growth in M3 money supply, its main policy indicator, was needed although the fact that M3 had exceeded its target this year was mainly due to a statistical overhang from 1996.
"From a current standpoint the Bundesbank considers a further weakening of money supply growth to be necessary for stability," the Bundesbank said in a statement.
German M3 grew by 6.4 percent in June, coming inside the Bundesbank's target of 3.5 percent to 6.5 percent for the first time.
The Bundesbank, issuing a statement after a council meeting which reviewed the M3 goal, also said it was sticking by its existing M3 target.
"As in the past, the Deutsche Bundesbank will check signals emanating from the development of the money supply in the context of a broad analysis of all data relevant to prices," the statement said.
"In doing this it will pay special attention to the external value of the deutsche mark and events on financial markets alongside data from the real sector," it added.
Referring to developments in M3 this year, the Bundesbank said: "The target was exceeded up to and including May of this year."

"The main reason for this was a large statistical overhang at the end of 1996 which resulted from high borrowing ahead of modifications to special rules on tax writedowns, especially for rented accommodation in east Germany, and the rise in property purchase tax."
